entry.title: Newsletter 03
entry.content:
It’s been an endlessly soft autumn in New York City, and a year since my last dispatch. Today I’m thrilled to release Unda Maris, an electronic audio device I’ve developed over the last year. You can read more about it on Metalabel, where I have copies for sale from the edition of 25.

I won’t say too much about it here, save for the fact that it’s a work that’s difficult to place its point of genesis exactly. Perhaps it began when I first learned about the Gateway Process and the CIA-funded research into the military applications of remote viewing. Or when I walked into a medieval church in Tours on a hot July afternoon four years ago and listened to an organist rehearsing a fragment of a song; the song still unknown to me but the breadth of its reverberations still lodged in my neurons. Or perhaps it was when I stepped into Alvin Lucier’s classroom on my first day of college, a composer whose music I’m still metabolizing after all these years.

However it began, I’m excited to be sharing it after a year in development, and I’ll be hosting a launch/listening party with Ergot Records on Thursday, December 3rd. I hope to see some of you there!

I’ll also continue to sell non-editioned ceramic objects on my web shop, where I have a new section for incense trays. These flared and floating forms perhaps echo Lucy Rie’s bowls and the conical design of audio speakers (see also the Japanese tradition of monkō, “listening to incense”). I’ve also been experimenting with a variation on the same form, adding a snip of nichrome wire that works as a post for candles.

Separately from the processes of object-making, I’ve been an ambivalent about the presentation of product images. I recently read Janet Malcolm’s collection of memoir essays, Still Photos, in which she describes her early career at The New Yorker writing shopping guides without the accompaniment of images.

Image generated using Janet Malcolm’s description of a desk by Hans Wegner in 1966.

The indexical function of the product image is relocated into the latent space of content navigated by language itself, which can prompt an image from an LLM more consistently than into the mind of the reader. On Shopify’s evergreen page on developing MVPs, the early deployment of marketing materials is recommended as a means of validating the product’s market before investment in production, a strategy enabled by the prevalance of dropshipping, industries of white-label production, and the normalization of crowdfunding.

In the migration of the product image from proof of life to proof of sale, they become image-products: speculative objects freely floating in economies of goods and attention. As minor egregores of consumer desire, these images are free to exist without a destiny bound to material substrate, and only sometimes dropshipped into reality once the weight of their stochastic gradient descent plunges them down into meatspace. In online “dopamine shops,” the sustain-release cycle of dopamine is choreographed by simulating the shopping experience entirely. These images have an existence like medieval birds of paradise, which were thought to live in the clouds surviving on atmospheric dew alone, until death.

“Thus, in adult life, the quest is not to possess the object; rather the object is pursued in order to surrender to it as a medium that alters the self” – Christopher Bollas, The Shadow of the Object: Psychoanalysis of the Unthought Known (1987).

That’s it for now — see you next time!

entry.title: Newsletter 02
entry.content:
A brief ceramics update: I’ll be selling some wares as part of a pop-up sale curated and hosted by Pyperbleu in Williamsburg. Open Sat-Sun August 23-24 from 12-6pm, with a reception at 3pm Saturday.

“Thus the miniscule, a narrow gate, opens up an entire world. The details of a thing can be the sign of a new world,” writes Bachelard in The Poetics of Space. Taken somewhat literally, the travel vases I’ve been making over the years have led me to some bigger pieces this year. Earlier this summer I exhibited a new sculptural work, After Orpheus, for a show at Millenium Film Workshop curated by Michèl Saint-Michel. And in the Pyperbleu show, I’ll be debuting the first of a series of lamps.

My shop page is currently sold out, and I’m in the process of redesigning the page a bit. But in the meanwhile, I’ll have new pieces available for sale at a temporary shop page https://shop.reubenson.com starting 12pm EST on September 1st.

Listening Station

entry.title: Newsletter 01
entry.content:
In conversation I sometimes joke that I’ve finally entered my verbal phase of development. Whereas my creative efforts in the past have been directed towards (wordless) music and ceramics, the impetus for this inaugural newsletter is to announce three recent pieces of writing (not including this newsletter itself).

I’m still sorting out what writing means to me, but that said, I do know that I resist Vilém Flusser’s claim that the written word is a linear medium. I frequently have the following experience: within the first ½ second of encountering a block of text, I already know if it contains a specific word of interest before I’ve “read” anything; and then it is when I linearly scan the text that I confirm its exact location within the text. You might associate this phenomenon to the larger practice of speed reading (which I cannot do).

In the context of writing, the operational modality of contemporary LLMs gestures towards this in another way. Token generation is linear, but works within an n-dimensional latent space of possible token generations.

My mental model of contemporary culture tends to fall back into a fundamental hypothesis about the DJ as archetypal figure, one that simultaneously assembles an audience and creates a socio-cultural context. The USB stick they arrive with is the latent space from which linear temporality is structured just-in-time.

In the larger context of the creator economy, the more successfully you refine your latent space, the more you subject yourself to audience capture. The perennial adage “you are what you eat” involves a reciprocal axiom: you eat what you are.

Somewhere within this ouroboros of corpus and hallucination, writing, like all non-linear media, may be a strategy for enacting the autophagic ritual of delimiting latent space.

News

Every year gets shorter the older I get. But each winter stays the same, which means each year is proportionally more winter. This last winter I listened to Jessica Pratt’s Here in the Pitch almost every day, but to my ears, nothing screams transition to spring louder than Khan Jamal’s Infinity; aside from the peeping of frogs, of course.

Quiet Time - My essay on background music and environmental attention has been published online by Are.na Editorial as part of the Naive Yearly series.

Airs - A collection of poems accompanied by recordings of the wind has been published in the Spring 2025 issue of The HTML Review. I’ve also written a bit more background on this project here.

Surface Tension - My essay on the aesthetic experience of surfaces was published in the 2025 Are.na Annual which is available for purchase and you can download a PDF of my essay individually here.

And to return to my original impetus for starting this newsletter, I’ve added a few more items to my online ceramics shop. I’m finally getting back in the ceramics studio, so stay tuned for a bigger shop update later this year.
